location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
location.notes: Represents the Swedish universities where students were recruited; travel destinations (Central Africa/Indian peninsula) captured separately in subcohort.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers given in main text; Table S1/S4 (supplementary) may contain per-subject data but not provided here.

sample_id.notes: No sample-level identifiers given in main text.

subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Two travel-destination subgroups defined the cohort structure.

control.notes: Study design is a before/after travel comparison, not a case-control study; no explicit control/case labeling provided.

country.evidence_quote: 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs
country.notes: Country of residence/origin of participants; specimens collected before and after travel while residing in Sweden.

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return
days_from_first_collection.notes: Reported as median/range for before and after timepoints (study-level aggregate), not resolvable to a single per-sample day count without fabrication.

westernized.notes: Not explicitly labeled in the paper, though participants are Swedish (implicitly Western); not stated as such.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.

age.notes: Only a range is reported, not a single mean/median age value; captured in age_min/age_max instead.

age_group.notes: Age range 23-34 falls entirely within Adult category (18-65) per schema definition; not explicitly labeled 'Adult' in text.

sex.evidence_quote: with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35)
sex.notes: Aggregate cohort-level sex distribution, not per-sample; not split by travel destination subgroup.

age_years.notes: Only a range (23-34 years) reported, not a single per-subject age value.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to entire cohort at both before and after sampling timepoints; also confirmed in Discussion ('none of the subjects took antibiotics before or during travel').

disease.notes: Cohort described as healthy exchange students; travelers' diarrhea reported as a transient trip-related symptom (69% incidence) rather than a formal disease classification, so left not_reported to avoid over-interpretation.

disease_details.notes: Study population is healthy Swedish students traveling abroad; no disease/condition is explicitly assigned in text.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment response/tumor context in this paper.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: As many as 69% of subjects (12/17 in the Central Africa group and 12/18 in the Indian peninsula group) had travelers' diarrhea
feces_phenotype.notes: Interpreted travelers' diarrhea as a stool-related clinical phenotype reported for the cohort; exact ontology mapping uncertain.

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Specific agents (mefloquine, proguanil, atovaquone) mentioned in Discussion as antimalarial agents used by subjects; none took antibiotics.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: most prominently for genes encoding resistance to sulfonamide (2.6-fold increase), trimethoprim (7.7-fold), and beta-lactams (2.6-fold)
biomarker_name.notes: Ordered to align with biomarker_value and biomarker_unit lists.

biomarker_value.notes: Corresponding fold-change values for antibiotic resistance gene categories (sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactam) after travel.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: As many as 69% of subjects (12/17 in the Central Africa group and 12/18 in the Indian peninsula group) had travelers' diarrhea
feces_phenotype_value.notes: 69% computed as reported directly; matches feces_phenotype 'Travelers' diarrhea'.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Field not applicable to this study (not an oncology paper).

study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier (e.g., 'AuthorX_Year' format) was reported in the text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the provided paper text; paper_id supplied externally as 26259788.

target_condition.evidence_quote: we used explorative shotgun metagenomic sequencing to address the abundance of >300 antibiotic resistance genes in fecal specimens
target_condition.notes: Study investigates acquisition of antibiotic resistance genes and ESBL-producing bacteria in travelers; both aspects are primary phenotypes studied.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction method not specified in main text; likely detailed only in supplemental material, which was not provided.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
sequencing_platform.notes: A separate platform, Illumina MiSeq, was used specifically for sequencing ESBL-positive bacterial isolates ('DNA was extracted from ESBL-positive isolates and sequenced using the Illumina MiSeq instrument'), but the primary metagenomic sequencing platform was Illumina HiSeq.

host_species.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

extraction_warnings: This paper does not provide per-subject or per-sample metadata tables in the main text (Table S1-S4 are supplementary and not included), so subject_id, sample_id, and several demographic fields could not be extracted at sample_level; granularity was set to subgroup_level based on the two travel-destination cohorts (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula).
Age is reported only as a cohort-wide range (23-34 years) and sex as an aggregate percentage (74% female), not stratified by subgroup or individual.
Fields such as westernized, disease, bmi, ancestry, lifestyle, and body_site_details are not explicitly reported in the available text.

This paper concerns gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene changes after travel, not a disease/cancer or clinical treatment-response study; most schema fields (disease staging, ORR, PFS, OS, neonatal, obgyn, smoker, HLA) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
feces_phenotype and feces_phenotype_value were inferred from mention of travelers' diarrhea as the closest stool-related phenotype reported; exact ontology alignment is uncertain.

treatment field includes antimalarial chemoprophylaxis agents (mefloquine, proguanil, atovaquone) mentioned as medications used by study subjects during travel, not a therapeutic intervention for a disease.

biomarker_name/value/unit fields were derived from reported fold-change increases in resistance gene categories (sulfonamide, trimethoprim, beta-lactam), interpreted as quantifiable biomarkers of the gut resistome; this mapping is an interpretive choice given the study's non-clinical nature.

study_name and pmid could not be extracted from the provided text; these fields are marked as not_reported despite being required.
dna_extraction_kit was not described in the main text and may be present only in supplemental material, which was not provided for extraction.

Two sequencing platforms were used in this study (Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomic sequencing and Illumina MiSeq for bacterial isolate sequencing); only the primary metagenomic platform (HiSeq) was selected for the single-value 'sequencing_platform' field.

target_condition was inferred from the study's overall aims rather than a single explicit disease/condition label, as this is primarily a microbiome/resistome surveillance study rather than a disease-focused clinical study.
